The **Finance (No. 2) Act 2010** is a UK legislation that received Royal Assent on **8 April 2010**, just before the general election that year. It was the second Finance Act of 2010 (following the **Finance Act 2010**, which was enacted earlier in the same fiscal year). The Act introduced several tax measures, many of which were contested due to the political context of the time (a hung parliament and the transition from a Labour to a Conservative-Liberal Democrat coalition government).

### **Key Provisions of the Finance (No. 2) Act 2010**
Here’s a detailed breakdown of its major components:

---

### **1. Income Tax Changes**
- **Personal Allowances**:
  - The **personal allowance** (the amount of income tax-free) was increased for those under 65:
    - **2010-11**: £6,475 (from £6,035 in 2009-10).
    - The Act laid the groundwork for further increases in future years.
  - The **higher-rate threshold** (above which 40% tax applied) was frozen at **£43,875** (down from £43,000 in 2009-10 due to indexation).

- **50% Additional Rate Introduction**:
  - A **new 50% income tax rate** was introduced for earnings **over £150,000** (effective from **6 April 2010**).
  - This was a Labour government measure to increase taxation on high earners.
  - The **personal allowance was gradually withdrawn** for those earning over £100,000 (reducing by £1 for every £2 earned above this threshold).

- **Restriction of Tax Reliefs for High Earners**:
  - Pension tax relief for those earning **over £150,000** was restricted (phased in from 2011-12).
  - The **annual allowance** for pensions was gradually reduced from £255,000 to £50,000 (fully implemented in later years).

---

### **2. National Insurance Contributions (NICs)**
- **Increase in NIC Rates**:
  - **Class 1 (Employee NICs)**:
    - Main rate (12%) remained, but the **upper earnings limit** was aligned with the higher-rate income tax threshold.
  - **Class 4 (Self-Employed NICs)**:
    - The **main rate increased from 8% to 9%** (from April 2011).
    - The **additional rate (2% above the upper limit) was introduced**.
  - **Employer NICs**:
    - The **secondary threshold** (point at which employers start paying NICs) was frozen at £136/week.

- **One-Year NIC Holiday for New Businesses**:
  - A temporary ** NIC holiday** for new businesses (up to 10 employees) in certain regions (outside London, the South East, and the East of England).
  - Exempted employers from paying **up to £5,000** in NICs for each new employee hired in the first 12 months.

---

### **3. Corporation Tax Changes**
- **Main Rate Adjustments**:
  - The **main corporation tax rate** was **reduced from 28% to 27%** (from April 2011).
  - The **small profits rate** was **reduced from 21% to 20%** (from April 2011).
  - The **lower and upper limits** for small profits rate eligibility were adjusted.

- **Bank Levy Introduction**:
  - A **new bank levy** was introduced on the **global balance sheets** of UK banks and building societies (as well as foreign banks with UK operations).
  - The levy was **0.05% per year** on liabilities (excluding certain items like retail deposits).
  - This was part of post-financial crisis measures to recoup bailout costs.

- **Controlled Foreign Company (CFC) Rules Reform**:
  - The Act began the process of reforming **CFC rules** (fully implemented in later Finance Acts) to make the UK more attractive for multinational businesses.

---

### **4. Value-Added Tax (VAT)**
- **Standard VAT Rate Reversion**:
  - The **temporary reduction in VAT from 17.5% to 15%** (introduced in the 2008 Financial Crisis recovery measures) **ended on 1 January 2010**.
  - The Act **restored VAT to 17.5%** and later **increased it to 20%** (from 4 January 2011 under the coalition government).

---

### **5. Capital Gains Tax (CGT) Changes**
- **Entrepreneurs’ Relief Extension**:
  - The **lifetime limit for Entrepreneurs’ Relief** (which taxes qualifying gains at 10%) was **increased from £1 million to £2 million**.
  - The **holding period** for qualifying assets was **extended from 1 year to 2 years**.

- **CGT Rate Increase for Higher Earners**:
  - The **CGT rate increased from 18% to 28%** for higher-rate taxpayers (from 23 June 2010).
  - Lower-rate taxpayers continued to pay **18%** (or 10% for Entrepreneurs’ Relief).

---

### **6. Stamp Duty Land Tax (SDLT)**
- **Temporary SDLT Holiday Ended**:
  - The **temporary increase in the SDLT threshold for residential properties** (from £125,000 to £175,000) **expired on 31 December 2009**.
  - The Act **reinstated the standard £125,000 threshold** from 1 January 2010.

- **First-Time Buyer Relief**:
  - A **new relief** was introduced for **first-time buyers** purchasing properties **under £250,000** (effective from March 2010 to March 2012).
  - This exempted them from SDLT on such purchases.

---

### **7. Anti-Avoidance and Compliance Measures**
- **Disclosure of Tax Avoidance Schemes (DOTAS) Expansion**:
  - The Act **extended the DOTAS regime** to cover more tax avoidance schemes, including those involving **inheritance tax, stamp duty land tax, and annual tax on enveloped dwellings (ATED)**.

- **General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) Precursors**:
  - While the full **GAAR** was introduced later (in the **Finance Act 2013**), this Act included measures to **strengthen HMRC’s powers** against aggressive tax avoidance.

- **Penalties for Careless Errors**:
  - Increased penalties for **careless inaccuracies** in tax returns.

---

### **8. Alcohol, Tobacco, and Fuel Duties**
- **Increases in Excise Duties**:
  - **Alcohol duties** were increased:
    - **Beer duty** rose by **2% above inflation**.
    - **Wine and spirits duties** also saw above-inflation increases.
  - **Tobacco duties** were increased by **1% above inflation**.
  - **Fuel duty** was **frozen** (despite planned increases), but a **1p increase** was scheduled for later (later deferred).

---

### **9. Other Notable Measures**
- **Furnished Holiday Lettings (FHL) Tax Relief Restrictions**:
  - The Act **restricted loss relief** for FHL businesses, aligning them more closely with mainstream property businesses.

- **ISA Limits Increase**:
  - The **annual ISA allowance** was increased to **£10,200** (from £7,200), with **£5,100 allowed in cash ISAs**.

- **Inheritance Tax (IHT) Nil-Rate Band Freeze**:
  - The **IHT nil-rate band** (threshold before tax applies) was **frozen at £325,000** until 2014-15.

---

### **10. Political and Economic Context**
- **Pre-Election Measures**:
  - The Act was passed in the **wash-up period** (the final days before Parliament dissolved for the 2010 general election).
  - Many measures (like the 50% tax rate and NIC increases) were **Labour policies** that the incoming **Coalition government (2010-2015) later modified or reversed**.
  - The **VAT increase to 20%** (implemented in January 2011) was a **Coalition decision**, not part of the original Labour plan.

- **Controversies**:
  - The **50% tax rate** was highly debated, with critics arguing it would **discourage investment** and **lead to tax avoidance**.
  - The **bank levy** was seen as a way to **recover costs from the 2008 bailouts** but was criticized for not going far enough.

---

### **11. Subsequent Changes & Repeals**
- **50% Tax Rate**:
  - The **Coalition government reduced it to 45%** in the **Finance Act 2012** (effective April 2013).
- **NIC Changes**:
  - Some NIC increases were **modified or delayed**.
- **VAT**:
  - The **20% rate remained** (and is still in place as of 2024).
- **Bank Levy**:
  - The levy **evolved into the Bank Surcharge** (8% on profits from 2016).

---

### **Where to Find the Full Text?**
The **Finance (No. 2) Act 2010** can be read in full on:
- **[UK Legislation.gov.uk](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2010/8/contents)**
- **[HMRC Guidance Notes](https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/finance-act-2010)**

---
### **Summary of Key Takeaways**
| **Area**               | **Major Change** | **Effective Date** |
|------------------------|------------------|-------------------|
| **Income Tax**         | 50% rate for earnings >£150k | April 2010 |
| **Personal Allowance** | Increased to £6,475 | April 2010 |
| **NICs**              | Class 4 rate → 9% (2011) | April 2011 |
| **Corporation Tax**   | Main rate → 27% (2011) | April 2011 |
| **CGT**               | Rate → 28% for higher earners | June 2010 |
| **VAT**               | Reverted to 17.5% (then 20% in 2011) | Jan 2010 / Jan 2011 |
| **Bank Levy**         | 0.05% on liabilities | 2011 |
| **SDLT Relief**       | First-time buyer exemption (under £250k) | March 2010 |
